prompts.code.explain.detailed: Explain this [language] code for [level]: first one sentence on what it does, then line by line. Point out non-obvious parts and possible failures with unusual input. Don't rewrite the code. Code: [code]
prompts.code.explain.refine: Line [number] is still unclear. Show with an example what happens to the data [example] there.
prompts.code.explain.check: Here's how I understand this code: [my explanation]. What did I miss?
prompts.code.plan.detailed: I need to build: [task] in [language or platform]. Constraints: [constraints]. Make a plan of small steps that can each be tested on their own. For each step: what to do, how to test it, which mistakes are likely. Don't write code yet.
prompts.code.plan.refine: Step [number] is too big. Split it into 3 smaller ones.
prompts.code.plan.check: What should I clarify with the client or teacher before starting?
prompts.code.causes.detailed: This [language] code should [expected behaviour], but [what happens]. List possible causes from most to least likely. For each, say how to check it with one simple action. I've replaced keys and passwords with placeholders. Code: [code]
prompts.code.causes.refine: I checked cause [number], it's not that. Here's what I saw: [result]. What next?
prompts.code.causes.check: Explain how I could find this kind of bug myself next time.
prompts.code.minimal.short: Reduce this code to a minimal example that reproduces the error: [code]
prompts.code.minimal.detailed: Here's a code fragment and the full error text. Help me reduce the code to a minimal example that reproduces the same error. Explain what you removed and why. I've replaced keys and passwords with placeholders. Code: [code] Error: [error text]
prompts.code.minimal.refine: The error doesn't reproduce in the minimal example. What that you removed might matter?
prompts.code.minimal.check: Write a short problem description for a forum question based on the minimal example.
prompts.code.tests.detailed: Suggest test cases for this [language] function: normal input, boundary values, empty input, wrong type, very large values. Table: “input — expected result — what it checks”, then write the tests in [framework]. Function: [code]
prompts.code.tests.refine: Test [number] passes even though the function is wrong. How do I make it stricter?
prompts.code.tests.check: Here are my tests: [tests]. Which important cases did I miss?
prompts.code.message.short: What does this error message mean? [error]
prompts.code.message.detailed: Explain this [language] error message in plain words: what it means, which line it points to, and the common causes. Don't fix the code for me; tell me where to look. Error: [error] Code fragment: [code]
prompts.code.message.refine: I found the line but can't see the problem. Here it is with the variable values: [data].
prompts.code.message.check: I think the error is caused by [my guess]. Does the message text support that?
prompts.code.approaches.short: Compare two approaches to the task: [approach 1] and [approach 2]
prompts.code.approaches.detailed: For the task [task] in [language], compare [approach 1] and [approach 2]. Table: readability, speed, memory use, maintenance difficulty, typical mistakes. Given the constraints [constraints], say which to choose and when the choice would change.
prompts.code.approaches.refine: Show a short code example for each approach so I can see the difference.
prompts.code.approaches.check: I chose [approach] because [reason]. Are there risks I haven't considered?
prompts.code.readme.short: Draft a README for this project: [description]
prompts.code.readme.detailed: Draft a README for the project: [description]. Sections: what it is, how to install, how to run, configuration (environment variables without real values), how to test, known limitations. Use only facts from the description; where data is missing, mark it [fill in].
prompts.code.readme.refine: Add a “Common problems” section based on these errors: [errors].
prompts.code.readme.check: Read the README as a beginner: where would they most likely get stuck?
prompts.code.readability.short: How can I make this code easier to read? [code]
prompts.code.readability.detailed: Review this [language] code for readability: variable and function names, function length, repetition, comments, magic numbers. List the issues as “where — what's wrong — better option”, then give an improved version. Don't change behaviour. Code: [code]
prompts.code.readability.refine: Explain issue [number] in more detail: why is it better for someone reading the code a year later?
prompts.code.readability.check: I rewrote the function: [code]. Is it clearer, and is the behaviour unchanged?
prompts.code.secrets.short: Which lines in my code look like secrets I shouldn't share?
prompts.code.secrets.detailed: I'm about to show code to an AI or publish it. Explain how to find and replace secrets in it: API keys, tokens, passwords, database connection strings, personal data. Suggest a placeholder format (e.g. YOUR_API_KEY) and how to keep real values in environment variables on [language or platform]. I'm not sending the code itself.
prompts.code.secrets.refine: I accidentally published a key. What should I do first?
prompts.code.secrets.check: Give me a short “before sending code” checklist of 5–7 items.

verify.code.explain: Run the code with different inputs and check that the behaviour matches the explanation.
verify.code.plan: A plan is a hypothesis. Start with the smallest step and check that it works before moving on.
verify.code.causes: Test hypotheses one at a time: add value logging or use a debugger rather than changing everything at once.
verify.code.minimal: Run the minimal example and confirm it produces the same error.
verify.code.tests: Run the tests: they should fail on wrong code and pass on correct code.
verify.code.message: Find the line number and file name in the message and look there yourself before changing code.
verify.code.approaches: If speed matters, measure on your own data: the AI's estimates are a guide, not a measurement.
verify.code.readme: Follow the README on a clean machine or in a new folder: every command must work.
verify.code.readability: Run the tests after edits: improving readability must not change behaviour.
verify.code.secrets: Look through the code once more yourself: keys, tokens, passwords, database URLs and personal data must be replaced.
